detail:
MedlinePlus describes allergic rhinitis management as combining avoidance of the allergens that trigger symptoms with medicines chosen for the pattern and severity of symptoms. Sources describe reducing exposure to pollen, dust mites, mold, and animal dander where possible, and note that pollen counts tend to be higher on hot, dry, windy days, which shapes when seasonal symptoms are most likely.

Medicine classes in the sources include antihistamines, nasal corticosteroid sprays, described as the most effective treatment for allergic rhinitis, antihistamine nasal sprays, and decongestants for a runny or stuffy nose, along with nasal saline washes that help remove mucus. MedlinePlus also describes allergen immunotherapy, given as allergy shots or as tablets or liquid under the tongue, as a longer-term approach that can make a person less sensitive to specific allergens over time. Follow-up in the sources centers on symptom control and on allergy testing when the triggers are not clear.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing allergic rhinitis.
summary: MedlinePlus outlines allergic rhinitis treatment as allergen avoidance plus medicine classes including antihistamines and nasal corticosteroid sprays, with saline washes and allergen immunotherapy described for longer-term control.
takeaways: avoiding identified allergens is a foundation in the sources
nasal corticosteroid sprays are described as most effective
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Allergic rhinitis: medicines, nasal sprays, and allergen avoidance
